name: Duskhollow

stars.name: Duskhollow
stars.notes: Quiet, long-lived K-class star with remarkably low flare activity, steady and dependable

planets.name: Kindling
planets.notes: Small volcanic body in a tight orbit, tidal forces keep its interior molten despite its size

planets.name: Heatherdown
planets.notes: Tidally locked habitable world, terminator zone supports temperate forests and grasslands, population 45 million

planets.name: Grainfield
planets.notes: Dry world with shallow aquifers, population 3.8 million in agricultural dome settlements extracting subsurface water

planets.name: Brume
planets.notes: Frozen world with thick haze of sublimating nitrogen, occasionally visited by ice harvesters

asteroid_belts.name: Dustling Belt
asteroid_belts.notes: Thin belt of small rocky bodies, minimal mining value but used for target practice by local militia

stations.name: Hollow Gate
stations.notes: System's sole significant station, handles trade, customs, and communications relay for the outer frontier

faction_control.notes: Small-scale democratic local government, technically within Frontier Marches jurisdiction but largely self-governing due to distance

history: Surveyed in 2398 by a long-range frontier probe, the system was marked as habitable but low-priority due to its remote location at the edge of settled space.
A small colony ship of agrarian settlers arrived in 2521, drawn by Heatherdown's abundant land and Duskhollow's stable, predictable star.
Duskhollow has remained quiet and largely overlooked for over a century, its residents content with self-sufficiency and minimal contact with the wider galaxy.
description: Duskhollow earns its name from the perpetual amber twilight that defines life in this system. The aging K-class star casts everything in warm orange tones, and on tidally locked Heatherdown, the terminator zone exists in a state of eternal sunset. Four small worlds orbit in a compact arrangement—volcanic Kindling closest in, then the two habitable worlds, and frozen Brume at the edge. It is a modest system, unremarkable in the grand catalog of stellar cartography, and its residents would tell you that's exactly the point.

Roughly 49 million people call Duskhollow home, almost all of them on Heatherdown or Grainfield. They are farmers, ranchers, and craftspeople who left busier systems behind for the promise of open land and quiet skies. Hollow Gate station handles the trickle of trade that reaches this far out—bulk grain exports, equipment imports, the occasional passenger. Life moves at its own pace here, governed by growing seasons and community meetings rather than galactic politics.

Duskhollow's isolation is both its charm and its vulnerability. The system sits at the very edge of the Frontier Marches, beyond which lies unsurveyed space. Heatherdown's residents have noticed an increase in unidentified ship transits over the past year—vessels that pass through without stopping or responding to hails. The Township Council has petitioned for a patrol frigate, but the request languishes in bureaucratic queues hundreds of light-years away. For now, the people of Duskhollow watch the sky with the same quiet patience they bring to everything else, and hope that whatever is passing through means them no harm.
